tasks.title: Pin the hull's side in AKnockedOutHullDoesNotFireAtAWreck
tasks.why: P2, WreckDecayTests.cs:500-537 (new). The test asserts an absence -- 0 Shot events from a knocked-out Tusk over 60 ticks -- and nothing in it shows a live hull would have fired, so two ways to a false green are open. The hull's spot is the first of +30z, -30z, +30x, -30x with open ground and sight of the wreck (:508), and only one of the four can reliably produce a shot: AtWreck fires only when InShadow returns non-zero (DirectFire.Wrecks.cs:168), and the shadow is the strip past the wreck on the shooter->wreck line no wider than Shelter.Body = WreckBlastReach * 0.5 * size = 1 m at scale 1 (:102). The three men stand at the trench centre, 2 m from the wreck along z (Hidden, :412-418): from +30x or -30x every one of them is about 2 m off that line and InShadow returns 0, and from the side of the wreck the men are not behind, t < 0 excludes them too (:206). In those cases the hull fires nothing whether KnockedOut is tested or not, the [N5.2] guard is gone and the test still reads green. The sibling tests added in the very same diff do carry the control the brief asks for (TankTests.cs:327-331 '[T32] setup: nobody was throwing grenades', WalkerArmamentTests.cs:84-94 the hurt flag), so this one is out of step with its own commit.
tasks.done_when: the test places the hull on the men's own side of the gun->wreck line (or asserts the chosen offset is one that puts the men in its shadow) and adds a setup assert that the same hull left live fires at the wreck at least once; it then goes red when the KnockedOut test is removed from AtWreck (DirectFire.Wrecks.cs:138), and WreckDecayTests stays green

tasks.title: Time WreckDecayTests and mark its whole-map runs Long
tasks.why: P2, WreckDecayTests.cs: not one [Category("Long")] in 775 lines, and this diff roughly doubles the sim it runs. New: HeOnlyTurnsOnTheWreckOnHisOwnScanTick 400 ticks (:540), AManOnTheWrecksFlankIsNeitherShelteredNorSuppressed 400 (:563), AManOffTheLineButInsideTheOldBodyIsNotKeptDown 400 (:589), ABlindingScreenOnTheLineDoesNotStopTheFireAtTheWreck up to 360 (:645), TheShelterListIsBuiltOnlyWhenAGunHasNoTarget 16 + 310 on two matches (:675). On top of the existing AnIdleMachineGunFiresAtTheWreck... 400 ticks on two matches in lockstep (:460), ARifleFiresAtItButDoesNotWearIt 400 (:472) and ALivingTargetAlwaysWins 300 (:481). Every one is a full CreatePlaytest battlefield. The rule is flat: a test over 3 s carries [Category("Long")] (workflow.md:261), and -EditOnly leaves the Long tier out precisely so the run before every commit of either lane stays under 300 s. Reading cannot settle a duration, so this is a measurement first; if these are over 3 s, every commit on the project is paying for about 3,000 ticks of battlefield that only the full gate needs.
tasks.done_when: an EditMode run reports each WreckDecayTests test's duration; each one over 3 s carries [Category("Long")] and the rest do not, the gate's -EditOnly time drops by what they cost, and the full gate stays green with no assert changed

tasks.title: Make the T28 garrison floor the ratio its comment promises
tasks.why: P3, TrenchSpreadTests.cs:276-281 and :364-368 (new). Both say the > 8 of 40 guard is 'raised to the sibling's 0.8 ratio', but what they compute is need = math.max(9, math.min(32, front.CellCount)). The min() hands the bound to the map: if the front trench has 12 cells the raised assert is 12 of 40 men, and the max(9) floor is literally the pre-T28 strength (> 8) it claims to have replaced -- so on a map whose front trench is small the test is no stronger than before while its message reads 'nearly the whole 40-man garrison reached a trench'. It also compares a man count to a cell count, which is the same thing only while one man stands per cell. Nothing here is wrong today; the guard is weaker than it reads, which is how a regression in the garrison search gets through a green run.
tasks.done_when: the floor is either a fixed 32 (the 0.8 ratio, with the measured cell count asserted as the premise that makes it reachable) or the comment is rewritten to say what min(32, CellCount) really guards; both tests stay green and go red when the garrison search radius is halved

tasks.why: P3, docs/reference/tasks.md:415-417 against WalkerArmamentTests.cs:80-84, :131-135 and UnitCatalogueTests.cs:41-55 (all new). The two archetype loops now hard-pin their own skipped sets -- Assert.AreEqual(38, occupied) and Assert.AreEqual(22, armoured), read off commit 46ef6bad9 -- and UnitCatalogueTests pins nine shipped numbers (rifleman 25/100, Maw 350/3600/1.6/600, Tusk 260/2000, officer aura 15).
